chunks: From him, from his father, from Jamil, from Zurarah, from Imam Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: Imam al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: 'Verily, when Allah, the Exalted, created Adam (peace be upon him) and breathed into him from the Spirit, the first thing he spoke was: "There is no god but Allah."'

So Allah, the Exalted, said: 'Have you turned away, O Adam?' He said: 'No, but I faced You with the word of Tawhid (Divine Unity).' He said: 'La ilaha illa Allah' four times, and its limit is ten, and its remembrance is twenty, and its glorification is twenty, and its declaration of oneness is twenty, and its takbir is twenty, and its praise is twenty, and its prayers are twenty, and its supplication is twenty, and its confirmation is twenty, and its confirmation is twenty, and its confirmation is twenty.' key_terms.لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: La ilaha illa Allah (There is no god but God)

ai.seo_question: What was the first thing Adam said after being created by God?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq highlights this narration to establish the primacy of *Tawhid* (monotheism) as the innate disposition (*Fitrah*) of humanity, linking Adam's first speech to the divine breath (*Ruh*). This event is interpreted by Shia scholars as the origin of the covenant (*Alastu bi Rabbikum*) and underscores that recognition of God is the foundational act of human existence, preceding all other knowledge or action.
